parse.title: Irritability
parse.wikitext:
<onlyinclude>'''Irritability''' is medically recognized as the pervasive and sustained emotional state of being easily annoyed and provoked to anger.<ref>{{cite journal|title=Glossary of Technical Terms|journal=Diagnostic and statistical manual of mental disorders (5th ed.)|year=2013|pages=824-5|doi=10.1176/appi.books.9780890425596.GlossaryofTechnicalTerms}}</ref> It may be expressed outwardly in the cases of violence towards others, or directed inwards towards oneself in the form of self-harm.<ref name="SnaithConstantopoulos1978">{{cite journal|last1=Snaith|first1=R. P.|last2=Constantopoulos|first2=A. A.|last3=Jardine|first3=M. Y.|last4=McGuffin|first4=P.|title=A clinical scale for the self-assessment of irritability|journal=The British Journal of Psychiatry|volume=132|issue=2|year=1978|pages=164–171|issn=0007-1250|doi=10.1192/bjp.132.2.164}}</ref> 

This effect, especially when strong, can sometimes cause violent or aggressive outbursts in a small subset of people who may be predisposed to it. The chances of somebody responding in such a way differs wildly between people and depends on how susceptible an individual is to irritability and how well they cope with it. It is also worth noting that this typically only affects those who were already susceptible to aggressive behaviours. However, regardless of the person, this effect results in a lower ability to tolerate frustrations, negative stimuli, and other people. A person undergoing this effect may be prone to lashing out at others, fits of anger, or other behaviours that would be uncharacteristic for them sober.

Irritability is often accompanied by other coinciding effects such as [[anxiety]], [[paranoia]], and [[ego inflation]]. It is most commonly induced during the [[duration#after effects|after effects]] of [[dosage#heavy|heavy]] [[dosage|dosages]] of [[stimulant]] compounds, such as [[cocaine]], [[methamphetamine]],<ref name="SommersBaskin2006">{{cite journal|last1=Sommers|first1=Ira|last2=Baskin|first2=Deborah|last3=Baskin-Sommers|first3=Arielle|title=Methamphetamine use among young adults: Health and social consequences|journal=Addictive Behaviors|volume=31|issue=8|year=2006|pages=1469–1476|issn=03064603|doi=10.1016/j.addbeh.2005.10.004}}</ref> and [[methylphenidate]].<ref>{{cite journal | vauthors=((Ahmann, P. A.)), ((Waltonen, S. J.)), ((Olson, K. A.)), ((Theye, F. W.)), ((Van Erem, A. J.)), ((LaPlant, R. J.)) | journal=Pediatrics | title=Placebo-controlled evaluation of Ritalin side effects | volume=91 | issue=6 | pages=1101–1106 | date= June 1993 | issn=0031-4005}}</ref> However, it can be a [[Substance withdrawal|withdrawal symptom]] of almost any substance, and can to a lesser extent present itself during [[alcohol]] intoxication.<ref name="NorströmPape2010">{{cite journal|last1=Norström|first1=Thor|last2=Pape|first2=Hilde|title=Alcohol, suppressed anger and violence|journal=Addiction|volume=105|issue=9|year=2010|pages=1580–1586|issn=09652140|doi=10.1111/j.1360-0443.2010.02997.x}}</ref></onlyinclude>
